skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
skill.summary: Guide agents to build distinctive, polished, production-grade frontend interfaces.
skill.author: AdamAugustinsky

security_audit.summary: The three static findings are false positives in design guidance text. No evidence found of system reconnaissance, prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, filesystem access, or command execution.

static_findings.snippet: This skill guides creation of distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "
- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like
- **Backgrounds & Visual Details**: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colo

finding_verdicts.reason: The line describes visual quality goals for frontend work, not collection of host, user, or environment details. No code or instruction requests system enumeration.
The line discusses font selection and avoiding generic font choices. It does not ask the agent to inspect installed fonts or system configuration.
The line recommends visual background effects such as textures and patterns. It does not direct probing of the host system or environment.

content.value_statement: Generic AI interfaces often look repetitive and miss the product context. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward polished frontend work with a clear visual direction.
actual_capabilities: Frames the purpose, audience, tone, and constraints before coding.
Chooses distinctive typography, color, layout, motion, and visual texture.
Encourages working HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, or Vue implementations.
Pushes components away from common AI design patterns.
Scales implementation complexity to match the chosen aesthetic.
limitations: It does not include executable helper scripts or design assets.
It depends on the host agent to inspect the existing codebase.
It gives design guidance, not automated visual testing.
It may need user constraints for strict brand or accessibility standards.

use_cases.title: Prototype A Product Screen
use_cases.description: Turn a rough interface idea into a visually distinctive screen that still supports real workflows.

use_cases.title: Upgrade A Web Component
use_cases.description: Refine an existing component with stronger typography, spacing, color, and interaction details.

use_cases.title: Explore A Visual Direction
use_cases.description: Generate a bold first pass for a landing page, dashboard, or application concept.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Simple Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a single web page for [product] using [framework]. Make it functional, visually distinctive, and aligned with [audience].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting from a basic product idea.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Existing UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component and redesign it with stronger hierarchy, spacing, typography, and motion. Keep the current framework and behavior intact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when improving a current component or page.

prompt_templates.title: Design System Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a compact visual system for [app type]. Define the mood, palette, typography choices, reusable components, and interaction style.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a project needs a coherent visual language.

prompt_templates.title: Full Experience Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a production-ready frontend flow for [workflow]. Include responsive states, meaningful transitions, loading and empty states, and a coherent visual concept.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when creating a multi-state interface or workflow.

output_examples.input: A SaaS dashboard needs a more memorable first screen.
output_examples.output: A redesigned dashboard with a strong visual theme, refined metrics hierarchy, responsive layout notes, and interaction behavior.
A clear art direction, distinctive typography plan, richer background treatment, and a polished first viewport that shows the product early.

output_examples.input: A React card component needs visual polish.
output_examples.output: A component brief covering layout, color, motion, hover behavior, empty state, and consistency with the existing app.

best_practices: Provide the product purpose, target audience, framework, and brand constraints before asking for implementation.
Ask for responsive behavior, accessibility expectations, and required states in the first prompt.
Review the result in a browser and request focused refinements for spacing, contrast, and motion.
anti_patterns: Do not use it when you need only backend logic or infrastructure changes.
Do not ask for generic beauty without explaining the user, workflow, or product context.
Do not accept decorative complexity that makes the interface slower, less readable, or less accessible.

faq.question: Does this skill write frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the agent to create working frontend implementations in common web frameworks.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing design?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current component or page and ask for targeted visual refinement.

faq.question: Does it include design assets?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance for frontend implementation and visual decisions.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for production projects?
faq.answer: The audit found no malicious behavior in the skill instructions. Review generated code before deployment.

faq.question: Can it follow a brand guide?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide colors, fonts, layout rules, and accessibility requirements in the prompt.
